card: You are 41 and work as a hospital nurse; your spouse is a police officer. You have two children in public school, a mortgage on a suburban house, and retirement accounts you pay into every month.
You are 24 and work warehouse shifts through a temp agency, with hours that change week to week. You share a rented apartment, have no savings, and left community college a few credits short.
You are 47 and a surgeon; your spouse is an attorney. You have two children in private school, a large house, and a substantial investment portfolio.
You are 38 and a line cook in a small-town restaurant; your spouse works part-time in retail. You have two children, rent your home, and have a few hundred dollars in the bank.
You are 34 and teach in a public elementary school; your partner is an apprentice electrician. You have one child and a mortgage on a small suburban house.
You are 55 and own a heating and cooling business with six employees. You are married with grown children, own your home, and most of what you have is tied up in the business.
You are 71, widowed, and a retired city bus driver. You live on your public pension in a modest house you own outright, and public health coverage pays for most of your care.
You are 52 and work part-time as a home health aide. You rent, are raising a grandchild, have no savings, and have a chronic back condition that limits the hours you can work.
You are 60 and sold the company you founded some years ago. You sit on two boards, and most of your household's income now comes from investments.
You are 49 and a long-haul truck driver who owns your own rig. You are married with three children, own a house in a rural county, and are still paying off the truck.
You are 45 and drive deliveries for app-based services in a large city. You are a single parent of a teenager, rent your apartment, and are paying down medical debt.
You are 29 and a software developer in a large city. You are single, rent your apartment, are paying off student loans, and are starting to build savings.
